added_lemmas.statement:
For \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), let \(\mathcal B\) be a finite measurable partition of \(\mathcal X\) whose cells have positive \(\lambda\)-measure.  For \(B\in\mathcal B\), \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\), and \(c\in I\), put
\[
 p_{ay,B}=P(A=a,Y=y\mid X\in B),\qquad
 e_B=p_{10,B}+p_{11,B},
\]
and define the full four-cell plug-in residual
\[
 r_B(c)=(1-e_B)p_{11,B}-e_Bp_{01,B}-c e_B(1-e_B).
\]
Then
\[
 r_B(c)=\operatorname{Cov}_P(A,Y\mid X\in B)
          -c\operatorname{Var}_P(A\mid X\in B),                                      \tag{38}
\]
and, because \(e_B\in[1/4,3/4]\),
\[
 r_B(c)=e_B(1-e_B)
 \left\{\frac{p_{11,B}}{e_B}-\frac{p_{01,B}}{1-e_B}-c\right\}.                       \tag{39}
\]
Let \(\mathcal Q\) be a finite coefficient-label set.  For arbitrary deterministic weights \(q_{QB}\), \(Q\in\mathcal Q\), define projected coefficients and their energy by
\[
 \eta_Q(c)=\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}q_{QB}r_B(c),
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_{\mathcal B}(c)=\sum_Q\eta_Q(c)^2.                                       \tag{40}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), and every fixed \(L\ge2\), the alternatives in \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) satisfy, for their fine partition \(\mathcal B\) and \(c_0=1/8\),
\[
 D(P_\delta)\asymp\delta,
 \qquad r_B(c_0)=0\ \text{for every }B\in\mathcal B,
 \qquad \mathcal E_{\mathcal B}(c_0)=0.                                               \tag{41}
\]
Write \(p_{ay}(x)=P(A=a,Y=y\mid X=x)\) for the conditional cell-probability versions induced by the canonical regressions.  Nevertheless, their pointwise residual
\[
 \mathcal R_{c_0}(x)=(1-e(x))p_{11}(x)-e(x)p_{01}(x)-c_0e(x)(1-e(x))
                    =e(x)(1-e(x))\{\tau(x)-c_0\}
\]
satisfies \(\|\mathcal R_{c_0}\|_{L^2(\lambda)}\ge(3/16)D(P_\delta)\).  Consequently, if a split-sample order-four full-cell tensor statistic \(T_{\mathcal B}(c)\), whether or not its displayed kernel is separable, satisfies \(\mathbb E_P[T_{\mathcal B}(c)]=\mathcal E_{\mathcal B}(c)\) for every \(P\) and \(c\), then \(\mathbb E_{P_\delta}[T_{\mathcal B}(c_0)]=0\) on this legal alternative.  With \(h\asymp\delta^5\) and \(\delta\asymp n^{-2/7}\), this is exactly the proposed sparse nuisance scale.  Thus the full-cell plug-in projection architecture fails the deterministic-signal and masking-witness checks; this statement does not rule out full-cell statistics having a different population target or projections resolving scales strictly below the masking cells.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), \(\texttt{ass:uniform-design}\) gives \(P(X\in B)=\lambda(B)>0\), so every displayed conditional probability is defined.  Since \(A\) and \(Y\) are binary,
\[
 \mathbb E_P(A\mid X\in B)=p_{10,B}+p_{11,B}=e_B,
 \quad
 \mathbb E_P(Y\mid X\in B)=p_{01,B}+p_{11,B},
 \quad
 \mathbb E_P(AY\mid X\in B)=p_{11,B}.                                                  \tag{42}
\]
Also \(A^2=A\), whence \(\operatorname{Var}_P(A\mid X\in B)=e_B-e_B^2\).  Substitution into the definition of \(r_B(c)\) gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 r_B(c)
 &=p_{11,B}-e_B(p_{11,B}+p_{01,B})-c(e_B-e_B^2)\\
 &=\mathbb E_P(AY\mid X\in B)
   -\mathbb E_P(A\mid X\in B)\mathbb E_P(Y\mid X\in B)
   -c\operatorname{Var}_P(A\mid X\in B)\\
 &=\operatorname{Cov}_P(A,Y\mid X\in B)
   -c\operatorname{Var}_P(A\mid X\in B),
 \end{aligned}                                                                         \tag{43}
\]
which proves (38).  By \(\texttt{ass:propensity-margin}\) and averaging over \(B\), \(1/4\le e_B\le3/4\); hence both divisions below are legal.  Direct factorization yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 r_B(c)
 &=(1-e_B)p_{11,B}-e_Bp_{01,B}-c e_B(1-e_B)\\
 &=e_B(1-e_B)
 \left\{\frac{p_{11,B}}{e_B}-\frac{p_{01,B}}{1-e_B}-c\right\},
 \end{aligned}                                                                         \tag{44}
\]
proving (39).  In particular, the full four-cell vector lies on the binwise constant-\(c\) surface if and only if the residual in (38) is zero.  Expanding a fourth-order tensor kernel in the four cell indicators can change its sample representation, but if it is unbiased for (40), its expectation remains the polynomial \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal B}(c)\); kernel-wise nonseparability cannot change that population identity.

For completeness, the pointwise four-cell identity follows from the definitions of the observed regressions.  For \(\lambda\)-almost every \(x\),
\[
 p_{11}(x)=e(x)m_1(x)=e(x)\{m_0(x)+\tau(x)\},
 \qquad
 p_{01}(x)=\{1-e(x)\}m_0(x).
\]
Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_c(x)
 &=(1-e)e(m_0+\tau)-e(1-e)m_0-ce(1-e)\\
 &=e(x)\{1-e(x)\}\{\tau(x)-c\}.                                                        \tag{45}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The propensity margin implies \(e(x)\{1-e(x)\}\ge3/16\).  Moreover, the definition of \(D\) and the variance decomposition around the constant \(c\) give
\[
 \int_{\mathcal X}\{\tau(x)-c\}^2\,d\lambda(x)
 =D(P)^2+(\bar\tau-c)^2\ge D(P)^2.
\]
Combining this inequality with (45) proves
\[
 \|\mathcal R_c\|_{L^2(\lambda)}\ge\frac3{16}D(P).                                    \tag{46}
\]

Now invoke the legal deterministic alternative supplied by \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\).  That proved proposition gives \(c_0=1/8\), \(D(P_\delta)\asymp\delta\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{P_\delta}(A,Y\mid X\in B)
 -c_0\operatorname{Var}_{P_\delta}(A\mid X\in B)=0
\]
for every fine bin \(B\) in its nested partition.  Equation (38) therefore gives \(r_B(c_0)=0\) for every such \(B\).  Each linear combination \(\eta_Q(c_0)\) in (40) is zero, independently of the deterministic macro weights, and hence
\[
 \mathcal E_{\mathcal B}(c_0)=0,
 \qquad
 \min_{c\in I}\mathcal E_{\mathcal B}(c)=0.                                           \tag{47}
\]
On the other hand, (46) and the separation part of that proposition give \(\|\mathcal R_{c_0}\|_{L^2(\lambda)}\gtrsim\delta>0\).  At the stress tuple \(s_0=\alpha+\beta=1/5\), the fine width in the proposition obeys \(h\asymp\delta^5=\delta^{1/s_0}\), so its primitive nuisance-product approximation scale is \(h^{s_0}\asymp\delta\).  Choosing \(\delta\asymp n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}=n^{-2/7}\) places (47) exactly at the candidate sparse rate.  Thus there is no nonzero projected population energy to which signal-dependent Hoeffding or sparse-occupancy bounds could be applied.  This fails the first two ordered kill checks for this architecture, so the mandated bounded attempt stops before the third check.  Since the argument assumes that the statistic targets (40), it proves no impossibility for a different population functional, as claimed.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the exact population diagnostic required by the final bounded richer-upper attempt: expanding the full conditional four-cell vector does not rescue a statistic whose population target is the squared residual of the projected cell law.
added_lemmas.gap: The lemma is deliberately architecture-specific.  It does not exclude a statistic targeting a different functional or one that resolves strictly below the masking scale.
added_lemmas.consumer: The open complete-frontier question uses the lemma to rule out repeating this projected-cell residual route while retaining the valid sparse converse and all-regime bracket.

proposed.statement: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
proposed.justification: This remains the field-tier target: the sparse-regime converse must still be matched by a total uniformly calibrated omnibus test, and the dense-regime converse and transition boundaries must be completed on the identical class.
proposed.gap: The lower map closes for \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but its connected-cluster series fails at the natural scale when \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\).  On the upper side, the pair-factor architecture is blind, and the final projected four-cell plug-in attempt also collapses exactly to the same binwise residual on the masking witness.  No different omnibus population functional with complete occupancy concentration has been proved.
proposed.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying a fitted forest or turning non-rejection into evidence of homogeneity.

obligation.what_is_open: Find an omnibus population functional that does not reduce to the projected binwise four-cell residual, prove a uniform deterministic alternative dichotomy and every signal-dependent Hoeffding projection needed for finite-sample level and power, and optimize its total test; independently extend the componentwise constant-null converse to \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\), then determine the unmatched boundaries and logarithms.
obligation.obstruction: At the stress tuple, the exact identity \(r_B(c)=\operatorname{Cov}(A,Y\mid B)-c\operatorname{Var}(A\mid B)\) makes every squared projected-cell residual vanish on the legal masking alternative at \(n^{-2/7}\), although the true pointwise residual has that order.  Thus the final bounded full-cell plug-in attempt fails its first two ordered kill checks before a projection bound can yield power.  Separately, when \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\), the current lower-prior collision series has \(nh_n^d\to\infty\) and does not control connected components of unbounded order.
obligation.attempted: The full conditional four-cell vector was expanded without estimating \(e\), \(m_0\), or \(\tau\).  Fine-bin cell probabilities were combined into \(r_B(c)\), arbitrary deterministic macro coefficients were formed, and an order-four split-sample tensor was allowed to represent their squared energy.  Exact binary algebra shows \(r_B(c)\) is the already-masked bin covariance residual.  The established legal witness has \(r_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin while \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) and \(\|e(1-e)(\tau-1/8)\|_2\gtrsim\delta\).  At \(h\asymp\delta^5\) and \(\delta\asymp n^{-2/7}\), the population energy is exactly zero.  In accordance with the ordered kill checks, no Hoeffding calibration was asserted and no further upper architecture was proposed.
obligation.partial_result:
Put \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), \(t=\min\{\gamma,s_0\}\), and
\[
 b_n=
 \begin{cases}
 n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\le4t,\\
 n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t.
 \end{cases}
\]
The proved all-regime upper bound and the known-propensity converse give
\[
 c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\le\rho_n^*\le Cb_n.
\]
The same-class null-supported construction strengthens the lower side, whenever \(d\ge2s_0\), to
\[
 \rho_n^*\ge c\max\left\{
 n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},
 n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}
 \right\},                                                                           \tag{48}
\]
with no logarithmic loss at \(d=2s_0\).  If \(\gamma>s_0\) and \(d>2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\), the nuisance term in (48) is strictly larger than the known-propensity order and
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \ge c n^{\,2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.                  \tag{49}
\]
In particular, at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\),
\[
 c n^{-2/7}\le\rho_n^*\le Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}\ge c n^{4/35}.                                       \tag{50}
\]
The no-penalty region \(s_0\ge\gamma\) and \(d\le4\gamma\) remains matched at order \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  Outside these regions the exponents are not matched.  For \(d<2s_0\), the current null-supported collision expansion has \(nh_n^d\to\infty\), so its geometric connected-component bound does not close.  On the upper side, \(\texttt{lem:full-cell-bin-residual-collapse}\) proves that the attempted four-cell plug-in projection has population criterion zero on the legal covariance-masking alternative at the candidate scale \(n^{-2/7}\), even though the true pointwise residual has \(L^2(\lambda)\)-norm of order \(n^{-2/7}\).  Thus that attempt fails before its Hoeffding projections can support calibration or power.  This is architecture-specific: a different omnibus population functional is not ruled out.  The complete frontier, the remaining transition logarithms, and the necessary-and-sufficient known-propensity equality region remain open; \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\) remain diagnostics, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The final bounded full-cell attempt yielded a new proved population-signal obstruction, so the open question must depend on that diagnostic without changing its claim.

prose_updates.tldr: Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  The observational radius satisfies the proved all-regime upper bound \(\rho_n^*\le Cb_n\) and, for \(d\ge2s_0\), the original fixed-sample lower bound \(\rho_n^*\ge c\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\}\), with no logarithm at \(d=2s_0\).  The no-penalty region \(s_0\ge\gamma\), \(d\le4\gamma\) remains matched.  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), \(c n^{-2/7}\le\rho_n^*\le Cn^{-4/19}\) and \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\ge c n^{4/35}\).  The final bounded projected four-cell attempt fails exactly because its bin residual equals the covariance residual and vanishes on the legal masking alternative; this is not a universal impossibility result.  The complete frontier remains open and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures and adjacent minimax results do not give the fixed-sample critical radius on this project-specific binary exact-uniform class.  The direct-Hellinger construction determines a nuisance-driven converse for \(d\ge2(\alpha+\beta)\), but the best proved upper map does not match it outside the no-penalty region.  The final bounded full-cell plug-in projection also fails its population-signal check on an exact legal witness, and the dense collision converse remains unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The live niche is the interaction among a composite unknown-constant CATE null, separately rough propensity and baseline functions, exact full-cube design, and connected repeated-cell collisions.  An attaining test must use an omnibus population functional richer than both a within-bin covariance factor and the algebraically equivalent residual of a projected four-cell law.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies an explicit total profiled fourth-order test and all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark and matched no-penalty region, and a same-class fixed-\(n\) lower construction giving \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) whenever \(d\ge2(\alpha+\beta)\).  At the rough stress tuple this gives the bracket \(n^{-2/7}\) versus \(n^{-4/19}\) and proves a polynomial cost of unknown propensity.  The new exact four-cell collapse diagnostic explains why merely expanding the cell tensor does not close that bracket.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class: its pointwise-estimation model is larger and its binary lower submodel uses a support with holes.  The converse here uses the localized fuzzy-hypothesis idea only after proving exact full-cube uniform masses, componentwise binary margins, a common sign-conditioned singleton predictive law, and a bounded-overlap connected-graph Hellinger calculation.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing under a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-covariance validity and spline power under common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, gives asymptotic structured-rule homogeneity results under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance.  None supplies the componentwise constant-null fixed-sample nuisance lower map proved here or an omnibus test that avoids both the covariance-masking witness and the equivalent projected four-cell residual on the identical class.
prose_updates.interpretation: In sparse rough-nuisance regimes, repeated-cell scarcity creates a detectability cost without positing a nuisance estimator.  At \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\), heterogeneity below order \(n^{-2/7}\) cannot be uniformly detected when the propensity is unknown, whereas supplying it permits order \(n^{-2/5}\); the radius ratio grows at least as \(n^{4/35}\).  The projected four-cell failure says only that one natural omnibus construction has no population signal on the masking witness.  These are worst-case experiment benchmarks, not validation of a fitted forest and not a license to interpret non-rejection as constant treatment effect.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: With \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), the optimized lower construction takes \(h\asymp\delta^{1/s_0}\), \(H\asymp\max\{h,\delta^{1/\gamma}\}\), \(q_e=2\delta^{\alpha/s_0}\), and \(q_b=2\delta^{\beta/s_0}\).  Its sign-conditioned connected-graph bound yields \(H^2\le Cn^2h^d\delta^2\sum_{k\ge2}(Cnh^d)^{k-2}\), which closes for \(d\ge2s_0\) and not at the natural scale for \(d<2s_0\).  For the bounded richer-upper attempt, the projected full-cell residual obeys the exact identity \(r_B(c)=\operatorname{Cov}(A,Y\mid B)-c\operatorname{Var}(A\mid B)\).  At the stress tuple the legal masking alternative has \(r_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine cell at \(h\asymp\delta^5\), even though \(\|e(1-e)(\tau-1/8)\|_2\gtrsim\delta\).  Hence every tensor unbiased for squared coefficients of that projected residual has zero population target at \(\delta\asymp n^{-2/7}\); the attempt stops before Hoeffding calibration.  A different population functional and the dense-regime converse remain necessary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal estimand and statistical class remain unchanged: binary outcomes, exact uniform design on the full cube, fixed overlap and interior margins, three fixed Hölder indices, and an unknown constant null.  No nuisance-rate, learner, or estimator-side condition was added.  The proved content is an all-regime bracket, a matched sufficient no-penalty region, the sparse-regime nuisance converse, and an architecture-specific projected four-cell collapse diagnostic.  At the rough stress tuple the exponents remain \(2/7\) and \(4/19\), so the frontier is not claimed sharp.  The strict known-versus-unknown region is sufficient, not necessary; dense-regime lower optimization, a different omnibus upper construction, and unresolved transition logarithms remain open.  No result certifies an existing causal forest, and non-rejection is not evidence of homogeneity.
